account: Today has mostly followed my appointments: office business, the mill inspection, lunch, council letters, tea at the east-bank cottage, and a return to the office, although I returned late. I am now with the secretary and builder; I am due home at seven. What is unusual is the vague talk of bridge or port changes. Freight said he had heard people mention changes, but supplied neither names nor a concrete plan. His warehouse was empty this afternoon, and he was seeking municipal delivery work. That could simply explain his interest; I have no evidence of a concealed undertaking. The builder completed the authorized two-emerald visual survey of the bridge and ferry landings. I paid him and read the signed report. He found no specific damage, and both routes were passable during his visit, but he did not certify structural safety or test lighting at night. He has offered a repair quotation, though the report identifies no confirmed defect requiring one. No repairs, alterations, or municipal deliveries are authorized. The secretary initially handed me the appointment book by mistake, then delivered the correct survey. She now holds the original appointments securely and says no council correspondence was available today. Her actions appear administrative; the book mix-up alone is not evidence of wrongdoing. Neighbour hosted tea, but I did not make out the later remarks and cannot claim to know their contents. I still want a specific source for the rumours and a concrete account of what changes anyone proposes. At present, routine efforts to find paid work and discussion of the survey are plausible explanations, not proof that something is happening behind my back.
